passage.title: En el mercado de la plaza
target: Turista: Buenos días. ¿Cuánto cuesta este melón?
Vendedora: El precio es de cuatro euros. Está muy dulce.
Turista: ¿Y cuánto cuestan dos limones?
Vendedora: Cada limón cuesta 1 euro.
Turista: ¿Cuánto es en total?
Vendedora: Son seis euros en total.
Turista: Perfecto. Me lo llevo todo, gracias.
native: Tourist: Good morning. How much does this melon cost?
Vendor: The price is four euros. It is very sweet.
Tourist: And how much do two lemons cost?
Vendor: Each lemon costs 1 euro.
Tourist: How much is it in total?
Vendor: It is six euros in total.
Tourist: Perfect. I will take it all, thank you.

words.note: Masculine: el melón, los melones. The written accent marks stress on the last syllable.
A small yellow or green citrus fruit; in Spanish it is masculine, so use el limón.
The amount asked for an item. In many places cuánto vale is also heard in shops.
The currency name stays the same in singular and plural: un euro, dos euros.
A place with stalls where people buy food and goods.
A woman who sells goods. The masculine form is vendedor.
The full amount after every item is added together.
A bag for carrying purchases. In shops it may cost extra.
A general word for fresh fruit sold at a stall.

words.en: How much does this melon cost?
words.note: A complete question for asking one price. Point to the item while you ask.

words.en: How much do two lemons cost?
words.note: Use cuestan because more than one item is being priced.

words.en: How much is it in total?
words.note: Asks for the sum of everything you have chosen.

words.en: I will take it, thank you.
words.note: Said when you decide to buy. Lo refers to the item already named.

words.en: Can you give me a bag?
words.note: Polite request; puede is the usted form of poder.

example.native: The melon costs four euros.

verbs.note: The stem changes o to ue in every form except nosotros, which keeps costamos.

example.target: Le pido dos limones, por favor.
example.native: I ask you for two lemons, please.

verbs.note: Used for requesting an item or an amount. The stem changes e to i in most forms.

example.native: Are you taking a bag?

verbs.note: In shopping, llevar means to take away the item you buy.

passage.title: Precios con céntimos en la panadería
target: Cliente: ¿Cuánto cuesta el pan?
Panadero: El pan cuesta 2,50 euros: dos euros con cincuenta céntimos.
Cliente: ¿Y el agua?
Panadero: El agua cuesta 1,20 euros.
Cliente: Entonces, ¿el total es 3,70 euros?
Panadero: Exacto. Los céntimos van después de la coma.
Cliente: Entiendo. Pago con un billete de cinco euros.
Panadero: Perfecto. Le devuelvo un euro con treinta céntimos.
native: Customer: How much does the bread cost?
Baker: The bread costs 2.50 euros: two euros and fifty cents.
Customer: And the water?
Baker: The water costs 1.20 euros.
Customer: So, is the total 3.70 euros?
Baker: Exactly. The cents come after the comma.
Customer: I understand. I will pay with a five-euro note.
Baker: Perfect. I will give you back one euro and thirty cents.

words.note: The smaller unit of the euro; one euro has one hundred cents.
In prices written in Spanish, the comma separates euros from cents.
The person who makes or sells bread in a bakery.
A shop that sells bread and other baked goods.
Often sold in bottles at small shops and kiosks.
The sum of all prices before you pay.
A person who buys goods or services.
A basic baked food sold by weight or by the loaf.
The currency unit; the plural is euros.

words.es: El pan cuesta dos euros con cincuenta céntimos.
words.en: The bread costs two euros and fifty cents.
words.note: Say the full amount in words when you want to be sure of the price.
Repeat the amount back to check it. Use the decimal comma shown on the price.

words.es: Los céntimos van después de la coma.
words.en: The cents come after the comma.
words.note: A clear way to explain how to read a price with cents.

words.es: Le devuelvo un euro con treinta céntimos.
words.en: I will give you back one euro and thirty cents.
words.note: Said by the seller when returning change.

words.es: Pago con un billete de cinco euros.
words.en: I will pay with a five-euro note.
words.note: Tells the seller which banknote you will use.

example.native: I give you back the change.

verbs.note: Stem changes o to ue. The Spanish verb takes a person as indirect object, so le refers to the customer.

example.native: I pay by card.

verbs.note: Pagar with con names the method; pagar en efectivo means to pay in cash.

example.native: The water costs one euro.

verbs.note: Costar is used for the price of an item or service.

passage.title: En el quiosco de la estación
target: Turista: Perdone, ¿cuánto vale esta moneda?
Dependienta: Es una moneda de dos euros.
Turista: ¿Y qué billete es este, el de diez euros?
Dependienta: No, este es un billete de cinco euros.
Turista: Necesito monedas de un euro para el autobús. ¿Tiene cambio de cinco euros?
Dependienta: Sí. Por su billete le doy tres monedas de un euro y una de dos.
Turista: Perfecto. Para el autobús son tres euros exactos, ¿verdad?
Dependienta: Sí, exacto. Gracias por su visita.
native: Tourist: Excuse me, how much is this coin worth?
Clerk: It is a two-euro coin.
Tourist: And which note is this, the ten-euro one?
Clerk: No, this is a five-euro note.
Tourist: I need one-euro coins for the bus. Do you have change for five euros?
Clerk: Yes. For your note I will give you three one-euro coins and one two-euro coin.
Tourist: Perfect. For the bus that is exactly three euros, right?
Clerk: Yes, exactly. Thank you for visiting.

words.note: A metal piece of money. Moneda also means currency in general.
A paper note of money, such as a five-euro note.
A small stand that sells newspapers, drinks and tickets.
A woman who works in a shop or kiosk. The masculine form is dependiente.
A large public vehicle that stops along a route.
The currency name used for coins and notes.
The number or sum of money you need or pay.
Used when a payment matches the price without change. It agrees with the noun it describes.
The coins or notes given back when you pay more than the price.

words.en: How much is this coin worth?
words.note: A natural way to ask a coin's value, common in shops and kiosks.
Asks for coins of a particular value.

words.en: That is exactly three euros, right?
words.note: Confirms the amount and invites the seller to agree.

words.en: Do you have change for five euros?
words.note: Useful when you need smaller notes or coins.
A common closing phrase in small shops.

example.target: Necesito dos monedas para el metro.
example.native: I need two coins for the metro.

verbs.note: Followed by a noun or by an infinitive: necesito pagar means I need to pay.

example.native: This note is worth five euros.

verbs.note: The first-person form is irregular: valgo. Use it for the value of a note or coin, not for the price of an item, which uses costar.

example.target: Le doy un billete de diez euros.
example.native: I will give you a ten-euro note.

verbs.note: Dar is irregular in the yo form: doy. Le doy means I give you, speaking to usted.

passage.title: ¿Efectivo o tarjeta?
target: Turista: Buenas tardes. ¿Aceptan tarjeta de crédito?
Camarero: Sí, aceptamos tarjeta para pagos de más de cinco euros.
Turista: ¿Y puedo pagar en efectivo si la cuenta es de cuatro euros?
Camarero: Claro, siempre aceptamos efectivo.
Turista: Entonces pago en efectivo, por favor.
Camarero: Perfecto. El café y el pastel cuestan cuatro euros.
Turista: Muy bien. Aquí tiene el dinero.
Camarero: Gracias. Le traigo el recibo ahora mismo.
native: Tourist: Good afternoon. Do you accept credit cards?
Waiter: Yes, we accept cards for payments over five euros.
Tourist: And can I pay in cash if the bill is four euros?
Waiter: Of course, we always accept cash.
Tourist: Then I will pay in cash, please.
Waiter: Perfect. The coffee and the cake cost four euros.
Tourist: Very well. Here is the money.
Waiter: Thank you. I will bring you the receipt right now.

words.note: Money in notes and coins. Pagar en efectivo means paying with cash.
A plastic payment card. Tarjeta de crédito and tarjeta de débito are different cards.
The amount owed in a restaurant or café.
A man who serves food and drinks in a restaurant. The feminine form is camarera.
The act or amount of paying for something.
A written proof that you have paid.
The machine on the counter that processes card payments.
A sweet baked dessert, often sold by the slice.
A hot drink made from coffee beans, and also the place that serves it.
A complete question to ask before ordering or paying.
Use puedo with an infinitive for a permission question.

words.en: I will pay in cash, please.
words.note: Tells the staff your choice before the bill is added.

words.es: Le traigo el recibo ahora mismo.
words.en: I will bring you the receipt right now.
words.note: Said by the waiter when the payment is finished.
A polite way to hand over payment.

example.native: We accept cards from five euros.

verbs.note: Aceptar is regular. A shop may accept some payment methods and not others, so ask before ordering.

example.native: Can you pay by card?

verbs.note: Poder changes o to ue. It is followed by an infinitive: puedo pagar means I can pay.

example.native: We pay in cash.

verbs.note: Pagar with en names the form of payment for cash; with con it names a card or note used to pay.

passage.title: Un billete grande en la tienda
target: Cliente: Buenas noches. Quisiera un zumo, por favor.
Dependiente: Muy bien. Son dos euros con cincuenta céntimos.
Cliente: Le doy este billete de veinte euros.
Dependiente: No tengo cambio de veinte. ¿Tiene algo más pequeño?
Cliente: ¿Me lo puede cambiar por dos billetes de diez?
Dependiente: Sí, se lo cambio ahora mismo. Aquí tiene diez y diez.
Cliente: Gracias. Entonces le pago el zumo con uno de diez.
Dependiente: Perfecto. Su cambio son siete euros con cincuenta céntimos.
native: Customer: Good evening. I would like a juice, please.
Shop assistant: Very well. That is two euros and fifty cents.
Customer: I will give you this twenty-euro note.
Shop assistant: I do not have change for twenty. Do you have something smaller?
Customer: Can you change it for me into two ten-euro notes?
Shop assistant: Yes, I will change it for you right now. Here are ten and ten.
Customer: Thank you. Then I will pay for the juice with one of the ten-euro notes.
Shop assistant: Perfect. Your change is seven euros and fifty cents.

words.note: A paper note of money. Use the plural billetes when you mean several notes.
The money returned when a payment is larger than the price.
A man who works in a shop. The feminine form is dependienta.
A drink made from fruit. In some regions jugo is used instead.
A place where goods are sold, usually smaller than a supermarket.
Used in greetings after dark, for example buenas noches.
The smaller unit of euro money. Cents follow euros with con or y.
A general word for an item or amount you have not named.
The plural of moneda. Coins are often given as change, so ask for them by value.

words.en: Can you change it for me?
words.note: Asks for change of a larger note in a polite form.

words.es: Le doy este billete de veinte euros.
words.en: I will give you this twenty-euro note.
words.note: Used to hand over payment and name its value at the same time.

words.en: I do not have change for twenty.
words.note: A shop worker's common reply when a large note is offered.

words.en: I will change it for you right now.
words.note: Le becomes se before lo: se lo cambio, never le lo cambio.

words.es: Su cambio son siete euros con cincuenta céntimos.
words.en: Your change is seven euros and fifty cents.
words.note: Said when the seller returns change after paying.

example.native: I can change this note.

verbs.note: Cambiar can mean exchange money or give change. Use the context to tell which one you mean.

example.native: I would like to ask for a juice.

verbs.note: In a shop, pedir means to ask for or to order the item you want.

example.target: Pago el zumo con un billete de diez.
example.native: I pay for the juice with a ten-euro note.

verbs.note: Pagar takes the thing paid for as its direct object and con for the means of payment.

passage.title: Contar el cambio en la cafetería
target: Sofía: Buenos días. Quiero un sándwich y un café.
Cajera: Son seis euros con cuarenta céntimos.
Sofía: Le doy un billete de diez euros.
Cajera: Aquí tiene el cambio: tres euros con sesenta céntimos.
Sofía: Cuento en voz alta: seis con cuarenta, y el resto es tres con sesenta.
Cajera: Exacto. Diez menos seis con cuarenta es tres con sesenta.
Sofía: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?
Cajera: Claro. Aquí lo tiene. Gracias por su compra.
native: Sofía: Good morning. I want a sandwich and a coffee.
Cashier: It is six euros and forty cents.
Sofía: I will give you a ten-euro note.
Cashier: Here is your change: three euros and sixty cents.
Sofía: I will count it out loud: six forty, and the rest is three sixty.
Cashier: Exactly. Ten minus six forty is three sixty.
Sofía: Can you give me the receipt, please?
Cashier: Of course. Here you are. Thank you for your purchase.

words.note: The money returned after a payment that is larger than the price. Usually said with the cashier counting it back.
A woman who takes payments at a till. The masculine form is cajero.
A filled bread snack. Pronounced with the stress on the first syllable.
A paper note of money. Say billete de diez euros for a ten-euro note.
The full amount you must pay after items are added.
The small unit of the euro; in amounts the cents follow the euros.
The arithmetic of taking the price away from the amount paid. Often used when checking change.
A paper or digital record that a payment was made.
A hot drink, and also the place that serves coffee.

words.es: Son seis euros con cuarenta céntimos.
words.en: It is six euros and forty cents.
words.note: Said by the cashier when giving the total with cents.

words.es: Le doy un billete de diez euros.
words.en: I will give you a ten-euro note.
words.note: Tells the cashier the note you will use for payment.

words.es: Cuento en voz alta el cambio.
words.en: I count the change out loud.
words.note: Lets the cashier hear your check before you leave.
The usual phrase when a cashier gives money back.

words.es: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?
words.en: Can you give me the receipt, please?
words.note: A complete polite request for proof of payment.

example.target: Cuento las monedas antes de salir.
example.native: I count the coins before leaving.

verbs.note: Contar changes o to ue except nosotros, which keeps contamos. It also means to tell a story.

example.native: Will you give me the change, please?

verbs.note: Dar is irregular in the first person (doy). Use the usted form da when speaking to a shop worker.

example.native: I want a coffee with milk.

verbs.note: Querer changes e to ie. Quiero is the usual way to order politely.

passage.title: Un recibo con fecha y precio
target: Señor Ortega: ¿Me da un recibo, por favor?
Empleada: Claro. ¿Qué datos necesita que aparezcan?
Señor Ortega: La fecha, el importe y la moneda, por favor.
Empleada: Aquí está. Fecha: 15 de noviembre. Importe: 18 euros.
Señor Ortega: ¿Cuál es el importe exacto del billete de ida y vuelta?
Empleada: Son 18 euros, y la moneda es el euro.
Señor Ortega: Está bien. Todo coincide con lo que pagué.
Empleada: Perfecto. Guarde el comprobante para cualquier cambio.
native: Mr. Ortega: Can you give me a receipt, please?
Clerk: Of course. What details do you need to appear?
Mr. Ortega: The date, the amount and the currency, please.
Clerk: Here it is. Date: 15 November. Amount: 18 euros.
Mr. Ortega: What is the exact amount of the return ticket?
Clerk: It is 18 euros, and the currency is the euro.
Mr. Ortega: That is fine. Everything matches what I paid.
Clerk: Perfect. Keep the proof of payment in case you change the trip.

words.note: A written record of a payment. Ask for it when you need proof.
The sum of money shown on a document or ticket.
The day, month and year printed on a receipt.
The type of money used in a payment; not the same as a coin.
A woman who works for a business. The masculine form is empleado.
A document showing that a payment was made. Common in Latin America.
A journey there and back; British English says return ticket. Ask for un billete de ida y vuelta.
Used when two amounts or details agree with each other.
A trip from one place to another.

words.en: Can you give me a receipt, please?
words.note: A polite request for proof of payment at a counter.

words.en: What details do you need to appear?
words.note: A clerk's question about what the receipt will show.
Reads the key details of a receipt in order.

words.es: Todo coincide con lo que pagué.
words.note: Confirms the check you have made against the receipt.

words.es: Guarde el comprobante para cualquier cambio.
words.en: Keep the proof of payment in case you change the trip.
words.note: Advice given when a document may be needed later.

example.native: Will you show me the receipt?

verbs.note: Mostrar changes o to ue except in nosotros, which keeps mostramos.

example.target: Reviso el importe antes de firmar.
example.native: I check the amount before I sign.

verbs.note: Revisar is regular. Use it when you verify details on a document.

example.target: Su nombre aparece en el recibo.
example.native: Your name appears on the receipt.

verbs.note: Aparecer is irregular in the first person: aparezco. It is used for information printed on a document.

passage.title: ¿Qué incluye la entrada?
target: Visitante: Buenos días. ¿El precio de la entrada incluye la audioguía?
Taquillera: No, la audioguía cuesta tres euros aparte.
Visitante: ¿Y la entrada ya incluye todos los cargos?
Taquillera: Sí, el precio incluye los impuestos y no hay otro cargo.
Visitante: Entonces pago la entrada y decido después sobre la audioguía.
Taquillera: Perfecto. La entrada cuesta doce euros.
Visitante: Aquí tiene. Gracias.
Taquillera: Disfrute de la visita.
native: Visitor: Good morning. Does the entry price include the audio guide?
Ticket clerk: No, the audio guide costs three euros separately.
Visitor: And does the entry already include all the charges?
Ticket clerk: Yes, the price includes the taxes and there is no other charge.
Visitor: Then I will pay for the entry and decide about the audio guide later.
Ticket clerk: Perfect. The entry costs twelve euros.
Visitor: Here you are. Thank you.
Ticket clerk: Enjoy your visit.

words.note: The ticket that lets you into a place, such as a museum or a show.
A woman who sells tickets at a counter. The masculine form is taquillero.
A device or app that explains a place while you walk around.
The amount asked for an item or entry.
A charge set by a government and added to some prices. Its name and rate depend on the country.
A charge or work done for a customer, shown separately in some bills.
An amount added to a price or bill. Use the plural cargos for several charges.
Describes an item already counted in the price.
A trip to see a place, such as a museum.

words.en: Does the price include the audio guide?
words.note: Ask this before paying to avoid an unexpected extra cost.

words.es: La audioguía cuesta tres euros aparte.
words.en: The audio guide costs three euros separately.
words.note: Said by the seller to show an item charged on its own.

words.en: Does the entry include all the charges?
words.note: Checks whether the total is the final amount.

words.en: I will decide about the audio guide later.
words.note: A clear way to delay a purchase while still paying for the entry.
A common polite closing phrase from staff.

example.target: La entrada incluye todas las salas.
example.native: The ticket includes all the galleries.

verbs.note: Incluir takes a y in some forms (incluyo, incluyen). Use it for what a price covers.

example.target: Disfrutamos de la visita al museo.
example.native: We enjoy the visit to the museum.

verbs.note: Regular. Usually disfrutar de: disfrutar de la visita. Disfrute is the usted command, a polite closing.

example.target: Decido después de ver el precio.
example.native: I decide after seeing the price.

verbs.note: Decidir is regular; the stem stays unchanged in every form.

passage.title: Un descuento en la librería
target: Ana: Hola. ¿Tiene algún descuento para estudiantes?
Dependiente: Para este libro no, lo siento.
Ana: ¿Y si compro dos libros?
Dependiente: Entonces tiene un 10 por ciento de descuento en el total.
Ana: Me parece bien. Llevo los dos.
Dependiente: Muy bien. Sin descuento son 26 euros; el total con descuento es 23,40 euros.
Ana: Gracias. Pago con tarjeta, si es posible.
Dependiente: Claro. Aquí tiene el recibo.
native: Ana: Hello. Do you have any student discount?
Shop assistant: Not for this book, I am sorry.
Ana: And if I buy two books?
Shop assistant: Then you get 10 percent off the total.
Ana: That sounds good to me. I will take both.
Shop assistant: Very well. Without the discount it is 26 euros; the total with the discount is 23.40 euros.
Ana: Thank you. I will pay by card, if that is possible.
Shop assistant: Of course. Here is the receipt.

words.note: A reduction in the usual price. Ask for it with tener un descuento.
A person who studies at a school or university.
A printed or electronic book sold in a bookshop.
A shop that sells books.
A lower price on an item, often shown on a sign.
A special price or promotion for a limited time.
Used with a number to say a share of the price, such as 10 por ciento.
A new item in a shop, often a new book or record.
The full amount after any discount is added or taken away.

words.en: Do you have any student discount?
words.note: A polite question to ask before the clerk sets the price.

words.en: If I buy two books, is there a discount?
words.note: Asks about a conditional offer before you choose.

words.es: Me parece bien. Llevo los dos.
words.en: That sounds good to me. I will take both.
words.note: Accepts an offer and confirms the purchase.

words.en: No, thank you. I prefer to buy one.
words.note: Declines the offer politely with a clear reason.

words.es: El total con descuento es 23,40 euros.
words.en: The total with the discount is 23.40 euros.
words.note: Confirms the final amount in euros and cents.

example.native: They have an offer this week.

verbs.note: Tener is irregular: tengo for yo, and e changes to ie in tienes, tiene and tienen.

example.native: I buy both books today.

verbs.note: Comprar is regular. Use comprar with the item and pagar with the means of payment.

example.native: It seems like a good price to me.

verbs.note: Parecer is irregular in the first person: parezco. Me parece is a common way to say you agree or like an offer.

passage.title: Un café en la estación
target: Teo: Buenas. ¿Cuánto son un café y una magdalena?
Dependienta: Son cuatro euros con cincuenta céntimos.
Teo: Perfecto. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
Dependienta: Lo siento, la terminal no funciona hoy. Solo aceptamos efectivo.
Teo: Entonces pago con un billete de cinco euros.
Dependienta: Gracias. Su cambio es cincuenta céntimos.
Teo: Cuento el cambio: cincuenta céntimos, correcto.
Dependienta: Muy bien. Espere un momento, por favor: le caliento la magdalena en el mostrador.
Teo: Gracias. Hasta la próxima.
native: Teo: Hello. How much are a coffee and a muffin?
Attendant: It is four euros and fifty cents.
Teo: Perfect. Can I pay by card?
Attendant: I am sorry, the card reader is not working today. We only accept cash.
Teo: Then I will pay with a five-euro note.
Attendant: Thank you. Your change is fifty cents.
Teo: I count the change: fifty cents, correct.
Attendant: Very well. Wait a moment, please: I will warm up the muffin for you at the counter.
Teo: Thank you. See you next time.

words.note: The surface where a worker takes orders or payments.
The machine that takes card payments.
Money in notes and coins, not card.
A small sponge cake, often sold with coffee in Spain.
A hot drink. Ask for café con leche for coffee with milk.
Money returned after a larger payment.
A paper note of money.
The small unit of the euro.
The full amount added together.

words.es: ¿Cuánto son un café y una magdalena?
words.en: How much are a coffee and a muffin?
words.note: Asks the total for two items with the plural form son.
Asks which payment method is accepted before you hand over money.

words.es: Lo siento, la terminal no funciona hoy.
words.en: I am sorry, the card reader is not working today.
words.note: Explains why a card payment cannot be made.

words.es: Entonces pago con un billete de cinco euros.
words.en: Then I will pay with a five-euro note.
words.note: Chooses the cash method and states the note.

words.es: Cuento el cambio: cincuenta céntimos, correcto.
words.en: I count the change: fifty cents, correct.
words.note: Confirms the change aloud before leaving.

example.native: The machine works well.

verbs.note: Funcionar is regular and used for machines, terminals and services.

example.target: Cuento el cambio antes de irme.
example.native: I count the change before I leave.

verbs.note: Contar changes o to ue, so the stem is cuent- in singular and plural forms except nosotros.

example.native: I wait a moment, please.

verbs.note: Esperar means to wait or to hope. Espere is the usted command form used by staff.
